study_identification_part.si_4_title: GPT-based normative models of brain sMRI correlate with dimensional psychopathology

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Four datasets were used: ABCD (Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study, n=11,031), ABIDE-II (Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange II, n=580), ADHD-200 (ADHD-200 Sample, n=922), and BHRCS (Brazilian High-Risk Cohort Study, n=737). ABCD was split into training, validation, and test sets. ABIDE-II, ADHD-200, and BHRCS were fully reserved for out-of-sample testing.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "The studied data include two datasets containing scores and diagnoses of psychiatric disorders, respectively: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD-200) and Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange II (ABIDE-II), and two neurodevelopmental studies containing measures of dimensional psychopathology: the Brazilian High-Risk Cohort Study (BHRCS) and Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD)"

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The ABCD dataset was split into three sets: training (n=6,756, TD subjects from lower 3 CBCL quartiles), validation (n=751), and test (n=3,524, including 10% normal CBCL + 100% high CBCL subjects). The normative model was trained exclusively on typically developing (TD) subjects from ABCD. ABIDE-II, ADHD-200, and BHRCS were fully reserved as out-of-sample test sets for clinical evaluation of ASD diagnosis, ADHD scores, and CBCL symptom groups respectively.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "The subjects of ABCD were split into three sets for training (n=6,756), validation (n=751), and testing (n=3,524) purposes." ... "The ABCD test set (n=3,524) and the complete datasets of ABIDE-II (n=580), ADHD-200 (n=922), and BHRCS (n=737) were reserved for the evaluation procedure (i.e., final tests)."

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model architecture was used, composed of a VQ-VAE and an ensemble of 9 GPT models. The training set consisted of n=6,756 TD subjects from the lower 3 CBCL quartiles of ABCD. The validation set had n=751 subjects. Overall (train + validation) = 6,756 + 751 = 7,507. The ABCD test set (n=3,524) includes both TD and high-CBCL subjects and was not used for model construction.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "The subjects of ABCD were split into three sets for training (n=6,756), validation (n=751), and testing (n=3,524) purposes." ... "we reordered the latent representations generated by the VQ-VAE to train multiple GPT models ... we had nine GPT models each obtained from a specific view of the serialized latent representations."

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The paper reports age statistics only for the entire ABCD dataset (mean 9.9 +/- 0.6 years, N=11,031) in Table 1, not separately for the training (n=6,756) or validation (n=751) subsets used for the normative model. The training/validation sets are subsets of ABCD (lower 3 CBCL quartiles), so the age distribution is expected to be similar (~9.9 +/- 0.6 years), but exact values for the normative model construction subset are not reported. The study selected subjects younger than 20 years of age. The ABCD study recruited children aged 9-10.

Since the training/validation sets are subsets of ABCD (lower 3 CBCL quartiles), the sex distribution may be similar but exact values for the normative model construction phase are not reported.
